items.title: Show HN: Port Zero – how I learned to stop worrying and love PORT=0
items.titleZh: Show HN：零号端口 – 我如何学会停止担忧并热爱 PORT=0
items.summary:
Hi HN, Recently I wasted several hours wrangling my dev environment only to find out that the browser frontend was talking to the wrong version of the backend. This got me thinking--why on earth are we still using simple numbers to describe which process to connect to? Why not use names instead? I thought of all the times a program wouldn't start because of port conflicts. The more I thought about it, the crazier it seemed. Modern operating systems already offer no-conflict ports: if you make your TCP server listen on port 0, the OS assigns you a random available port. But that only solves half the problem. I built the other half: PortZero. It's a GPLv3 program that watches for processes (and docker containers!) with a special PZ_TUNNEL environment variable: PZ_TUNNEL=myapp-{branch}.portzero.local:80 npm run dev

When it sees such a process or container, PortZero does this: 1. Create a virtual NIC (if it hasn't already) 2. Create a new virtual IP address 3. Create a DNS record that substitutes things like {branch} based on the working directory of the process, and points at that virtual IP address 4. Start listening on that virtual IP address on the port of your choice (e.g. port 80 for http, port 443 for https, port 5432 for postgresql) 5. Forward any TCP connections to that virtual IP address / virtual port to the random, OS-assigned port that your process or container is actually listening on The result is you don't have to think about ports anymore, you just have to think about subdomains. You can have multiple services available on port 80 without conflicts, as long as they have different portzero.local subdomains. It does some other cool stuff like: - Enable HTTPS on local HTTP services by creating a local CA and registering it on your machine - Enable cloud tunnels so you can access your apps on other devices (paid feature) Links: https://portzero.net/docs/ https://github.com/PortZeroNetwork/portzero

items.summaryZh:
您好，HN，最近我浪费了几个小时来整理我的开发环境，结果发现浏览器前端正在与错误版本的后端进行通信。这让我开始思考——为什么我们仍然使用简单的数字来描述要连接到哪个进程？为什么不使用名称来代替呢？我经常想到由于端口冲突而导致程序无法启动的情况。我越想，就越觉得疯狂。现代操作系统已经提供了无冲突端口：如果您让 TCP 服务器侦听端口 0，操作系统会为您分配一个随机可用端口。但这只解决了一半问题。我建造了另一半：PortZero。这是一个 GPLv3 程序，使用特殊的 PZ_TUNNEL 环境变量监视进程（和 docker 容器！）： PZ_TUNNEL=myapp-{branch}.portzero.local:80 npm run dev

当它看到这样的进程或容器时，PortZero 会执行以下操作： 1. 创建虚拟 NIC（如果还没有） 2. 创建新的虚拟 IP 地址 3. 创建一条 DNS 记录，根据进程的工作目录替换 {branch} 之类的内容，并指向该虚拟 IP 地址 4. 开始在您选择的端口上侦听该虚拟 IP 地址（例如，http 的端口 80、https 的端口 443、https 的端口 5432） postgresql) 5. 将任何到该虚拟 IP 地址/虚拟端口的 TCP 连接转发到您的进程或容器实际侦听的操作系统分配的随机端口。结果是您不必再考虑端口，只需考虑子域。您可以在端口 80 上使用多个服务而不会发生冲突，只要它们具有不同的 portzero.local 子域即可。它还有其他一些很酷的功能，例如： - 通过创建本地 CA 并在您的计算机上注册，在本地 HTTP 服务上启用 HTTPS - 启用云隧道，以便您可以在其他设备上访问您的应用程序（付费功能） 链接：https://portzero.net/docs/ https://github.com/PortZeroNetwork/portzero
